title: Traffic Slice Explorer — wireframes & grooming notes
content:
Purpose and context:
- Objective: sketch a compact console surface that lets platform owners and app developers slice traffic by API key, route, and time window to answer common questions: 
  * What keys are causing quota exhaustion?
  * Which route is driving burst costs?
  * Where do we need to add throttling or tiered limits?
- This doc is a brainstorm (wireframes + backlog grooming) for a new UI panel called Traffic Slice Explorer (TSE). Not final; intended to feed into next sprint refinement.

User personas for this surface:
- Platform Admin (SRE/product infra): wants to spot quota hotspots quickly and configure fallback/auto-scale policies.
- Product Owner (app team): wants per-key cost breakdown and historical usage to decide if a key should be moved to higher plan.
- Support/CS: triage customer tickets about rate-limit errors and find quick remediation steps.

High-level flows we need to support (priority order):
1) Investigate spike: choose time window -> isolate top keys -> drill into routes -> surface recent 429 spikes and recommended mitigations.
2) Monthly quota review: compare allotted vs consumed per-key across routes, export CSV for billing reconciliation.
3) Create/attach rules: from a problematic key/route view, create a quota override or scaled burst policy (can link to dedicated capacity).

Core components (sketch text descriptions):
- Slice bar (top): time window selector (quick presets: 1h/6h/24h/7d/30d), sampling granularity, and emergent-issue toggle (auto-highlights windows where error-rate > X).
- Primary canvas (left): stacked bar chart that shows token consumption broken down by key (color-coded), with hover showing route distribution for that time bucket.
- Details column (right): focused key/route card when a segment is clicked. Card shows: API key metadata, plan tier, quota (daily/monthly), tokens used, peak rps, 429 count, recent errors (last 1h). Controls: open quick actions (create temporary quota increase, create rule, mute alerts, export).
- Route breakdown mini-panel (below chart): top N routes for selected key/time slice, with sparklines, cost estimation, and suggested quantization/response-trim actions.
- Anomaly ribbon (above chart): small horizontal indicator highlighting buckets with unusual changes and link to auto-generated root-cause candidates (cache miss, new key, campaign spike).

Wireframe notes / interactions to validate in usability session:
- Clicking a legend color (key) should toggle visibility and optionally put that key into the detail card (not just hide).
- Multi-select keys to compare side-by-side in the details panel (up to 3).
- Right-click on a route row -> 'Pin as rule candidate' pre-populates a rule creation modal with route pattern + key + suggested limits.
- Export should default to CSV but have a JSON option for programmatic ingestion (supporting downstream billing/analytics).

Back-of-envelope data considerations (for engineering):
- Query size: per-customer keys may be thousands; UI query must be capped and paginated. Suggest server-side top-k aggregation by tokens and error-rate, return a compressed timeseries for top 50 keys only.
- Sampling: 1m resolution for <24h, 5m for 7d, 1h for 30d to bound response size.
- Perf SLO: initial load of TSE should be <1.5s for typical org (top-50 keys).

Edge cases & UX decisions:
- Keys with identical owners: show group toggle to collapse/expand.
- Missing metadata: anonymized keys should show "no owner" with a CTA to search internal id mapping.
- Extremely high-cardinality routes (patternized): collapse to route patterns using simple normalization (strip ids, timestamps). Provide a preview of normalization.
- Timezone handling: default to org timezone; allow user override per-session.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- TSE loads with time window presets and shows top-25 keys by token usage for that window.
- Clicking a key opens detail card with quota numbers and 429 count.
- Route breakdown shows top-10 routes for selected key + per-route token % and approximate cost.
- Quick actions: export CSV + open rule modal pre-populated.

Nice-to-have (post-MVP):
- Inline cost-savings recommendations (e.g., suggest low-precision embeddings, batching hints) per-route.
- Alert templates generated from the selected slice ("create alert for key X when 429s > 0.5% over 10m").
- Integration with Optimize to show quantization recommendations for heavy-cost routes.

Backlog grooming items (tickets suggested):
- PS-600: data API for top-k keys + sampled time-series (schema + perf budget).
- PS-601: UI component - stacked timeseries canvas + hover route detail popover.
- PS-602: details card UX + quick actions (rule + export).
- PS-603: route normalization library and preview endpoint.
- PS-604: anomaly ribbon backend: simple z-score detection + UI flags.

Mock copy / labels to iterate on in the next meeting:
- Page title: Traffic Slice Explorer
- Slice selector label: Window • Preset • Granularity
- Legend action: Compare | Pin | Export
- Detail card header: API Key • Plan • Last seen
- Route row actions: Pin as Rule • View Sample Request • Cost estimate

Research questions for user testing (3 quick tasks):
1) Given a sudden 20% cost increase in last 24h, find the top key and route likely responsible and export the data for billing.
2) For key K-123 (provided), open the details and create a temporary quota increase to unblock a customer. Note friction points.
3) Identify a route that would benefit from response-size reduction and note whether the suggested action feels actionable.

Open design/engineering tradeoffs to resolve in refinement:
- How much editing capability should details card have vs redirecting to full Quotas page? (MVP: quick rule drafts only).
- Should anomalies be calculated client-side for small windows to reduce backend work? (Pro: fast for ad-hoc; Con: inconsistent with server alarms).
- Export format: include raw tokens vs normalized cost units? (Prefer both with a default to tokens).

Next steps before grooming session:
- Samira: produce low-fidelity mockups for the three primary flows (investigate spike, monthly review, create rule) — due 2026-03-05.
- Ethan: scope PS-600 data API and give rough cardinality/perf cost estimate — due 2026-02-14.
- Maya: draft acceptance criteria for PS-601-PS-603 and prepare 3 user tasks for testing — due 2026-02-20.
- Liam: prototype route normalization examples and share a small dataset for UI demos — due 2026-02-18.

Notes / quick links to keep in the doc:
- Existing quota page: /product/console/quota-management (reference for linking).
- Current analytics endpoint: api/internal/usage/top-keys (will need extension).
